analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 16, 2026)
key_insights: A tech slump driven by AI worries is dragging US and APAC equities lower ahead of NVDA earnings (11/17) and a busy week of tech catalysts. US and EU equities still ended the prior week higher despite higher yields.

Broadening is the key theme. S&P 500 equal weight (SPW) and Stoxx 600 (SXXP) outperformed the cap-weighted SPX. The rotation into non-AI plays is extending on improved geopolitical prospects and growing AI concerns.
EU is a standout. Energy drove EU earnings strength, but median EPS growth matched the US at about 13% YoY. The share of EU companies beating EPS estimates in Q3 was above average.

India is a trade JPM is watching, helped by under-positioning, earnings acceleration, cheaper valuation, improving macro, lower oil and the need to diversify from the AI trade. Foreign buying is at a record but small relative to potential inflows given JPM's underweight stance.
Geopolitical catalysts this week include a Trump/Xi/Putin meeting on the APEC sidelines and EU foreign and defense ministers meetings. Brussels is reportedly proposing a new Ukraine loan.

Positioning Intel flows support broadening. Performance rebounded and de-grossing slowed. EU flows have risen +1.5z relative to US over 1-3 months, bringing relative EU positioning versus the US back to neutral.
Semis positioning has reset materially. The combined 6m positioning plus price z-score is near -3z. Hedge fund net flows in US semis were below -3z, AxJ was balanced and EMEA semis were bought.

NVDA focus is on guidance for next year's growth as the US Congress moves toward tighter AI chip export rules. JPM's Cembalest charts show a rising share of token consumption on Chinese open-weight models and about 1/3 of China's compute capacity located outside China.
JPM's APAC Tech, Innovation & Growth conference began today. Key focus points are AI capex growth, AI monetisation and physical AI. China tech earnings (BABA 11/19) also land this week.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. The regional preference stays long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation and Asia has pockets of both. Secular themes carry less weight within EU equities.

JPM thinks broadening can return, more clearly in the US than in the EU. EU earnings and positioning are supportive, but stability in EGB spreads is needed before broadening gains conviction in the EU.

Longs: tech and supercycle themes across infrastructure, less-levered hyperscalers and AI-vulnerables (AI and application software) rather than a pure semis-versus-software portfolio. Also cyclicals with a secular tailwind (EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners), EU Pharma and UKX in low vol, and selectively the consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerable names ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, challenged industries (autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech) and MDAX.
Option hedges to keep: MCX below UKX until clarity emerges on spending, pragmatism and ideology, and short France versus EU domestics on politics and dislocation.

Semis saw a sixth consecutive week of HF selling, the longest streak on record. Global HF net exposure is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025, and the global long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x. Retail flows suggested dip-buying and tech ETFs saw inflows.

A semis bounce similar to the one after the late-July momentum reduction is possible, but semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile since 2018. Because the 6m z-score of HF positioning is below the 6m z-score of relative returns, history suggests the rebound may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish.

Gross flows and HF performance stabilised. Thursday was the most positive global re-gross day in about a month. HF performance gained about 1.5% over five days and is roughly flat month to date. Europe is up 1.7% MTD and Asia is down 2%.

US positioning remains low, with the Tactical Positioning Monitor at the 20th percentile since 2015. Japan was broadly sold, with HF flows at -1.4z WoW and -2.3z MoM and all 11 sectors sold over the month. Combined Japan positioning is at the 24th percentile since 2015.

risk_factors: Renewed AI concerns and the tech slump, with NVDA earnings and China tech earnings this week.
Tighter US AI chip export rules, with a rising share of token consumption on Chinese open-weight models.
Instability in EGB spreads, which would hold back conviction in EU broadening.
Continued HF selling in semis. A rebound may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish.
The US is overheating, which is the basis for the regional preference over EU.
Geopolitical outcomes from the Trump/Xi/Putin meeting and EU ministers' meetings.
charts_described: Cembalest charts show a rising proportion of token consumption by Chinese open-weight models and that about 1/3 of China's compute capacity sits outside China.
vol_and_positioning: Global HF net exposure to semis is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025. The global semis long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x.
HF net flows in US semis were below -3z for the second week in a row. HF selling extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record.

Combined semis 6m positioning plus price z-score is near -3z. Global semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile versus data since 2018, so positioning is not especially low on a long-term basis.
HF gross leverage fell 4% week over week while net leverage was broadly unchanged. Thursday was the most positive global re-gross day in about a month.
US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 20th percentile since 2015. Europe rebounded faster from depressed levels, and relative EU versus US positioning is back to neutral.
Japan positioning is below average on a combined basis, at the 24th percentile since 2015, with HF flows at -1.4z WoW and -2.3z MoM.
Option hedges: keep MCX below UKX, and short France versus EU domestics.
geopolitical: Trump, Xi and Putin are due to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit on 11/19.
EU foreign ministers meet in Brussels on 11/16 to discuss Russia/Ukraine and the Middle East, and EU defense ministers meet on 11/17.
Brussels is reportedly proposing a new Ukraine loan.
The US Congress is moving to pass tighter AI chip export rules.
An EU-UK summit takes place in Brussels on 11/20.
Improved geopolitical prospects are cited as a support for the broadening trade.

tension_points.bull_case: EU earnings fundamentals are good, median EPS growth matched the US at about 13% YoY, and positioning is giving a buy signal.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro and thematics favor long US and Asia over EU, and secular themes carry less weight within EU equities. Broadening is seen coming back more clearly in the US.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lack of stability in EGB spreads, which JPM says is needed before broadening gains conviction in EU.

tension_points.bull_case: HF net exposure is down 67% from its peak, sentiment is very depressed, and the combined z-score near -3z preceded a bounce after the late-July momentum reduction.
tension_points.bear_case: Global semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile since 2018, and with HF positioning z-score below the relative-return z-score, history suggests the rebound may not be robust.
tension_points.what_invalidates: HFs continuing to sell and not turning more bullish, since the rebound may not be robust unless HF positioning z-score starts to rise relative to returns.
